newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks seesaw at open, CAC entrants rise.
newsitem.headline: French stocks seesaw at open, CAC entrants rise.

text.p: French stocks seesawed at the open of the Paris Bourse on Tuesday, dipping then rising with new entrants to the CAC-40 leading share index soaring and those making an exit dropping.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 6.19 points or 0.25 percent at 2,440.14 at 1000 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 2.5 points points at 2,438.5.
Volume was over 800 million francs in the first half-hour of trading.
Dealers said they were waiting for the 1330 GMT release of the U.S. fourth quarter employment cost index and January consumer confidence data, due at 1500 GMT.

On Monday, the SBF stockmarkets' association said insurer UAP, Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel and sugar maker Saint Louis would be dropped from the index and replaced by consumer goods company Bic, auto parts maker Valeo and insurer AGF.

Bic, Valeo and AGF were all higher, up 2.50 percent to 901 francs, 4.35 percent to 367.40 francs and 3.74 percent to 172 francs, respectively, and were all among the biggest gainers on the day so far.
UAP fell 0.21 percent to 141.20 francs, Eurotunnel was off 3.33 percent at 7.25 francs and Saint Louis dropped 3.16 percent at 1377 francs, drop as a result of the change.
Usinor Sacilor, once considered a candidate for the CAC, dropped 3.67 percent to 72.20 francs.
Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux both rose as rumours of a linkup, last floated in 1995, resurfaced after a French newspaper reported the idea was again being considered.
Another factor helping Suez was its announcement on Monday that it would post a 1996 profit of about 800 million francs and a rise in pre-tax, pre-exceptional results.

"Considered several times and regularly postponed, the last time in 1995, this operation is once again under review," daily Le Figaro said of the Suez-Lyonnaise linkup, citing sources close to the affair.
Suez and Lyonnaise spokeswomen said the groups' policy was not to comment on "rumours".
Suez rose 4.79 percent to 243 francs and Lyonnaise gained 3.18 percent, reaching 552 francs.
Moulinex rose after predicting improvement in its operating results despite drop in activity. Share was biggest gainer on the day, up 7.46 percent at 141.20 francs.

Societe Generale fell 1.94 percent to 608 francs after announcing the sale of two million shares of treasury stock at 610 francs a share. The sale represents 2.2 percent of Societe Generale's treasury stock.
